articles.title: Matt LaFleur shredded by Packers fans after team collapses vs Vikings
articles.summary: Matt LaFleur's decision to take points off the board in fourth quarter of eventual loss to Vikings is leaving Packers fans frustrated.
articles.body:
It's a new season for the Green Bay Packers but you couldn't tell based on what happened at U.S. Bank Stadium.

Matt LaFleur's Packers picked up right where they left off in blowing leads.

The Packers held a double-digit third-quarter lead, 22-10, against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Sept. 13, as they controlled the game from the beginning. You wouldn't know by looking at the final score.

The Packers not only lost, but were blown out in a disastrous finish, losing 39-22, as the Vikings scored the game's final 29 points.

Packers fans saw all of this last year, most notably in the team's wild-card epic collapse against the Chicago Bears when they allowed 25 fourth-quarter points. The Vikings outscored the Packers, 22-0, in this fourth quarter.

While it was a combination of events again that led to this meltdown, a decision that LaFleur made to take points off the board with the Packers ahead 22-17 early in the fourth quarter set the stage for this new collapse.

Trey Smack made a field goal to put the Packers ahead 25-17 but LaFleur decided to take 5 yards after a Vikings penalty instead of taking the three points. The Packers then faced a 4th and 1. He called a quarterback sneak and Love was stopped.

The Vikings went down and scored on the next possession. The momentum had changed and soon Collapse No. 1 in 2026 was complete.

Packers fans sound off on Matt LaFleur after loss to Vikings

articles.title: Green Bay Packers: “It’s on us” after 12 penalties in loss to Minnesota Vikings
articles.summary: Twelve flags for 98 yards. Five of them gave the Minnesota Vikings a first down. The Green Bay Packers were penalized four times as often as Minnesota at U.S...
articles.body:
Twelve flags for 98 yards. Five of them gave the Minnesota Vikings a first down. The Green Bay Packers were penalized four times as often as Minnesota at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday.

Minnesota was flagged three times for 15 yards in a 39-22 win.

Green Bay led 22-10 in the third quarter and outgained the Vikings 419-239 for the game.

Matt LaFleur told the team not to put it in the officials' hands

LaFleur got a question about three straight third-down penalties on one Minnesota drive.

"Yeah, it is," he said. "I mean, obviously, it had an effect because they were able to go down the score, and then we get the pick in the end zone. We get called for, was it DPI or holding? I don't know. I thought a lot of times that, like, you know, those plays happened down there, but they called it. So my point to the team is you can't put it in the hands of the officials."

Earlier in the same availability he had already gotten there: "Far too many penalties tonight."

Tucker Kraft and Christian Watson landed in the same place

Kraft, a captain for the first time Sunday, put the fourth quarter on Green Bay and nowhere else.

"Yeah, it's just a combination of mental errors and penalties," the tight end said. "I mean, in penalties, we're in control of our own actions. It's just we've got to clean that up. That's the only way we're going to grow as a program and be able to beat good teams."

Christian Watson, who scored both Packers touchdowns, was asked how much the penalties mattered.

"I mean, it was huge," Watson said. "I mean, we can't put stuff like that in the ref's hands. We've got to find a way to be disciplined and play sound football and avoid getting those things because I mean as much as you know anyone would want to argue each you know either way you know we put it in their hands I mean it's on us."

Safety Evan Williams framed it as a September problem that does not have to stay one.

"You see it a lot more early in the season," Williams said. "You know, just you see the impact of, you know, playing discipline versus not playing discipline and how that can change a game, you know, flip a game on its head."

Williams kept going, into the part that showed up in the fourth quarter.

"It's just, you know, doing the little things right, you know, just having the mental fortitude late in the game when you're tired, when it's late in drives to find a way to get off the field and do exactly what you're supposed to do," he said. "I feel like we put ourselves in a good spot, but at the end of the day, I said it before, but can't leave it up to the refs to make those type of calls. Just move forward. That's all you can do."

Matt LaFleur says the negative plays opened the floodgates

"When we got behind the sticks, if we had a negative play, a negative run, it just opens up the floodgates, and then it's a guessing game," LaFleur said. "Are they bringing it? Are they bluffing you? But that's the game they want to play."

Kraft said the same thing from the huddle's side of it. "And when we're constantly behind the sticks like that, that's where that defense thrives," he said. "And they took it to us."

Minnesota scored 22 points in the fourth quarter, three touchdowns inside a span of 2 minutes and 39 seconds. Green Bay was stopped twice on fourth down, lost a fumble and threw an interception.

Green Bay plays at the New York Jets on Sunday at noon CT.

articles.title: North Texas annihilates UNLV, 44-6, for Neal Brown’s first win
articles.summary: North Texas’ retooled roster decisively outplays a Mountain West contender in every phase.
articles.body:
In September 2025, the Washington State social media team tweeted a preview graphic for its upcoming game against North Texas . The graphic depicted a desert, an oil rig, saguaro cacti, and an eagle in a cowboy hat with a holster. The depiction of Denton could not be more detached from reality, but North Texas' fanbase decided to embrace the misrepresentation, and the eagle from the graphic — 'Desert Scrappy' — became a program icon, embroidered on Neal Brown's polo at his weekly press conference.

North Texas beat Washington State, 59-10.

One year later, the UNLV social media team tweeted a hype video set to Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" for its looming game against North Texas, also depicting Denton as a desert atmosphere.

Any time another program is unsure what Denton looks like, North Texas takes them sightseeing. And the No. 1 attraction the Mean Green show on this sightseeing tour is the lopsided scoreboard at DATCU Stadium.

The Mean Green obliterated UNLV by 38 points to record the first win of Neal Brown's coaching tenure. It was a thorough domination from start to finish and the Rebels were held out of the end zone for the first time since Sept. 18, 2021. Meanwhile, under the direction of new defensive coordinator Matt Powledge, North Texas prevented an FBS opponent from scoring a touchdown for the first time since Sept. 21, 2019.

Hours earlier on Saturday, roughly 230 miles north, a significant portion of North Texas' 2025 roster and coaching staff — now at Oklahoma State — upset No. 6 Oregon . That result showcased the sheer amount of talent the Mean Green lost from 2025 to 2026. But Saturday afternoon in Denton proved how well the program reloaded under Coach Brown. North Texas handled the preseason Mountain West favorite in every phase of the game.

Offensively, quarterback Tayven Jackson spread the wealth around in a performance featuring 233 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, and a rushing touchdown. Running back Jahiem White , who starred under Brown at West Virginia , looked fresh in his second game back from a knee injury, generating 124 rushing yards and a touchdown. With the former Big 12 starters leading the way, North Texas accrued 444 yards of offense against a UNLV defense which didn't allow more than 27 points in its first two contests.

Defensively, the Mean Green dominated the turnover battle, 4-0. North Texas, which accumulated the fifth-most takeaways in the FBS last season, continued the trend with a completely new staff and roster. Bryce Garza secured the lone interception of the game, while three different Mean Green players scooped up a fumble. The turnover creation was assisted by an assertive defensive line which registered four sacks against the Rebels, including 1.5 courtesy of UMass transfer defensive end David Onuoha.

Even on special teams, North Texas showed nothing but excellence in the Denton Desert. Kicker Dominic De Freitas sunk all three of his field goal attempts, producing the first six points of the game before North Texas fully settled in. From there, it was a steady beatdown, as North Texas unquestionably controlled the line of scrimmage on both sides.

UNLV (1-2, 1-0 Mountain West) is now 0-2 against the American Conference this season. The Rebels watched their Week 0 game against Memphis slip away in the second half, and this time, they weren't even in the same territory as their opponent. The inability to move the ball in the second half continues to plague UNLV, which has only scored 17 second half points in three games. These offensive struggles can be primarily attributed to the frontlines, as the Rebels were out-sacked by opponents, 10-2, in their two losses.

North Texas (1-1, 0-0 American) earned its first victory with Coach Brown and his significantly overturned roster. One week after playing respectably for a half against defending champion Indiana , North Texas found its full gear and obliterated what is expected to be one of the top teams in the Mountain West. The Mean Green now must return to the road and make a similar statement against a new Pac-12 team in Texas State.

articles.title: Green Bay Packers: Edgerrin Cooper has run out of patience with the finishing talk
articles.summary: Edgerrin Cooper gave reporters five sentences on Sunday and one of them was about being finished with the subject. The Green Bay Packers defense held Minneso...
articles.body:
Edgerrin Cooper gave reporters five sentences on Sunday and one of them was about being finished with the subject. The Green Bay Packers defense held Minnesota to 239 total yards, knocked Kyler Murray out of the game in the first quarter and intercepted his first pass. It then gave up 22 points in the fourth quarter of a 39-22 loss at U.S. Bank Stadium.

Cooper did not want to do the postgame version of this again.

Edgerrin Cooper: 'I don't want to talk about it no more'

"No, just correct the things we need to correct," Cooper said. "We didn't finish. I'm tired of saying this every time. I don't want to talk about it no more, but it's what we got to do. So we just got to figure it out."

Green Bay ran 21 times for 66 yards and did not score after the third quarter.

"I don't think it's a question of the guys we have in the room," right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele said. "I think it's more so, can we execute and make plays when you need them?"

The defense played well enough for most of three quarters

Minnesota ran 61 plays for 239 yards and averaged 3.9 per snap. The Vikings threw for 151 yards as a team. Green Bay got three sacks and an interception and forced Minnesota into a 38-yard field goal on its only first-half scoring drive that did not end in the end zone.

LaFleur said the flags, not the coverage, extended the drives that mattered.

"Yeah, I thought our defense played really well," he said. "You know, again, there were some unfortunate penalties we had that extended drives, and then I thought in the fourth quarter especially, offensively we put them in some really tough positions."

Green Bay was flagged 12 times for 98 yards. Five of those penalties gave Minnesota a first down. The Vikings were flagged three times all afternoon.

Carson Wentz replaced the concussed Murray in the first quarter and threw three touchdown passes, two of them to Justin Jefferson . T.J. Hockenson caught the other. Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason ran for scores in the fourth, and Minnesota converted a two-point pass to Jefferson to take the lead for good.

The pass rush is still waiting on Micah Parsons

Green Bay played without Micah Parsons, who is on the reserve/physically unable to perform list while he recovers from the torn ACL that ended his 2025 season and is ineligible to return before Week 5. Lukas Van Ness and the rest of the front got six quarterback hits.

CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson said during Sunday's broadcast that she asked Parsons whether he has Week 6 against the Dallas Cowboys circled. He left the date open and told her, "We will see," per Dallas Sports Journal.

Franklin's read on the opener was more forward-looking than Cooper's.

"We're not matching anybody's intensity, we set the tone for how we play," Franklin said. "Minnesota's just the first test. It's going to be good to put that on tape and let the league know what the Green Bay Packers defense is all about."

Safety Evan Williams put the fourth quarter on the details.

"Just having the mental fortitude late in the game when you're tired, when it's late in drives to find a way to get off the field and do exactly what you're supposed to do," Williams said. "I feel like we put ourselves in a good spot, but at the end of the day, I said it before, but can't leave it up to the refs to make those type of calls."

Green Bay plays at the New York Jets on Sunday at noon CT.

articles.title: Green Bay Packers: Christian Watson details what the team must fix after Week 1 Vikings loss
articles.summary: Christian Watson caught both of the touchdowns the Green Bay Packers scored on Sunday and did not want credit for either one. Watson took a Jordan Love throw...
articles.body:
Christian Watson caught both of the touchdowns the Green Bay Packers scored on Sunday and did not want credit for either one.

Watson took a Jordan Love throw 81 yards to the end zone with 7:54 left in the first quarter, then caught a two-yard score with 18 seconds left in the first half that sent Green Bay into the locker room up 19-10. The Packers led 22-10 in the third quarter and lost 39-22 at U.S. Bank Stadium.

"Didn't do enough for us to win the football game," Watson said. "Obviously it was super excited coming in from the first half, feeling like everything was going the right way, but it's hard to be proud of anything when it didn't amount to anything for the team. So it's a tough one."

Minnesota scored 22 points in the fourth quarter, three touchdowns inside a span of 2 minutes and 39 seconds. Watson said the room saw it coming and could not stop it.

"Yeah, the coach said it best," he said. "Momentum is a strong thing, and we didn't respond, so once they got that momentum, they just kept on going."

He also declined to hang the loss on Matt LaFleur's decision to take points off the board and go for it on fourth-and-1 in the fourth quarter.

"I don't think that one play was anything," Watson said. "I think there was a lot of plays that kind of escalated into the result of the game today. But I think in every situation, you've got to find a way to execute better. And once it comes down to execution and we didn't execute, we needed to."

Watson on finishing: 'The only answer is yes'

Finishing games was the offseason emphasis in Green Bay. Watson got the question everyone in the building knew was coming, and he did not dodge it.

"I think the only answer is yes after a result like today," Watson said. "I think it just comes down to execution. We've got to find a way to execute in those critical moments. We've got to find a way, all 11, to be on the same page on offense, defense, special teams, everything. It comes down to crucial moments in the game, and we've got to find a way to come out on top of those if we want to come out on top of the game."

On the penalties, of which Green Bay had 12 for 98 yards to Minnesota's three for 15, Watson went where Tucker Kraft and LaFleur went.

"It was huge," he said. "We can't put stuff like that in the ref's hands. We've got to find a way to be disciplined and play sound football."

One game into a season, Watson signed a long deal to be part of

Watson entered Sunday on a four-year extension worth a reported $92.5 million, one of several deals Green Bay handed out this offseason on a list that also includes Jayden Reed , Devonte Wyatt and, as of Saturday, Tucker Kraft .

He was asked how a team digests a loss like this with 17 games still in front of it.

"We've just got to be open to critiquing ourselves and being hard on ourselves," Watson said. "Because obviously it's only one game, but we've got to be able to learn from the mistakes, learn from the whole game, and find a way to come out on top. Otherwise, we don't want to turn the wrong direction. We want to find a way to get back to where we're at."

Love finished 21-of-42 for 387 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. Green Bay outgained Minnesota 419-239 and ran for 66 yards on 21 carries.

The Packers return to action against the New York Jets on Sunday at noon CT.

articles.title: Solheim Cup: How youthful Europeans helped Anna Nordqvist answer critics in win over US
articles.summary: Captain Anna Nordqvist's faith in Europe's young rookies paid off as they delivered crucial points in regaining the Solheim Cup with victory over the United States, writes Iain Carter.
articles.body:
Anna Nordqvist spoke in the build-up to the Solheim Cup about the European team being in a period of transition as she chose a line-up with four debutants.

Any fears about fielding rookies for the most pressure packed event in the women's game were proven unfounded in her team's thrilling 15-13 victory at Bernardus Golf last weekend.

Nastasia Nadaud (21), Julia Lopez Ramirez (23), Mimi Rhodes (24) and, eventually, Lottie Woad all delivered crucial points and gave an encouraging glimpse into Europe's future.

Three of the quartet were captain's picks, with the 22-year-old Woad the only debut automatic qualifier for the team that avenged defeat in Virginia two years ago.

"So many people said it was a bit of a risk having four rookies, but I was so impressed with them," Nordqvist said.

'Finally got our points' - Hull and Woad shine in European Solheim win

GB&I make history with first Walker Cup since 2015

Europe's skipper faced intense scrutiny throughout her captaincy, especially over her stubborn faith in Woad's partnership with fellow Englishwoman Charley Hull.

But she was ultimately vindicated, especially with her wildcard selections, which also included relative veteran Leona Maguire.

Between them they yielded eight and a half points, compared with five contributed by America's three captain's picks. Nordqvist's singles line-up also leant heavily on a willingness to trust in youth.

Of the youngsters tasting Solheim singles action for the first time only Rhodes failed to win and it took a brilliant performance from world number one Nelly Korda to beat her on the final day.

And the beaten Englishwoman had already contributed significantly alongside Nadaud with Friday fourball and Saturday foursomes wins that helped ensure 8-8 parity after the first two days.

In the singles Rhodes was sent out fourth, but it was positions six, seven and eight - Nadaud, Lopez Ramirez and Woad - that held so much significance to the final outcome.

All three delivered vital wins. "What people don't understand is they're so good when they come out on tour these days," Nordqvist said. "They just play fearless and they have so much personality.

"All of the four I had, I never felt like they were rookies. And the first day when I send out Nastasia and Mimi a lot of people questioned why would you send out two rookies, but I said why not. And they delivered.

"They delivered again on Saturday morning. And Sunday too. Mimi took Nelly down to 15. She's the number one player in the world, and she pushed her.

"Rookie Lottie making the winning putt. It's been really fun to have them and they bring out a fresh perspective.

"And I feel really old and I'm glad I'm retiring now because these girls are just so good."

'I said a few words' - Reid rallied Europeans

It fell to Woad to sink the putt that ensured Europe would win, with four matches still to be completed. Her 2&1 triumph over Auston Kim took Europe to 14 points with Carlotta Ciganda already unassailably three up on the 16th tee.

Europe were guaranteed to reach the magic number of 14½ points and there was nothing America could do about it. It should be noted, this was not a great US side with Korda, Alison Lee and Lauren Coughlin being head and shoulders above the rest.

Nordqvist's persistent faith in Woad and Hull, playing her two highest ranked players together in the four opening sessions seemed a folly. She insisted stats justified the call, but the partnership never gelled, yielding only half a point.

It was all the more jarring because elsewhere Nordqvist had unmistakably fostered that famed European spirit which so often permeates through Solheim and Ryder Cup successes.

It was crucial in overcoming Jennifer Kupcho's hammer blow long range birdies late on the Saturday evening that allowed the United States to force an unlikely share of the foursomes and fourball spoils.

All the momentum was with the visitors on the Saturday night, but it was soon washed away as the rain drenched Sunday singles began.

"We were on the team bus, I said a few words," said assistant captain Mel Reid of the aftermath of Kupcho's heroics. "The team bus is a special place for Team Europe.

"I think it's where we really unite, we really get together. We put the music on and it's a special place. I'm just glad there are no cameras there.

"But we got to the hotel and we put on a song, and I felt like it changed the mood and united us. It was weird.

"We just forgot what happened, the disappointment, and we just got back on it."

After a winless two days there was enormous pressure on Hull and Woad and the former barely missed a shot in an impressive 3&2 win over the tenacious Megan Khang.

The Englishwoman still could not buy a birdie putt on the slow greens but she never gave her opponent a sniff. Woad was equally strong and her decisive role at the end was in keeping with the spectacular start to her pro career.

There are no guarantees in golf, but in Woad, Nadaud, Lopez Ramirez and Rhodes Europe appear to have an exciting nucleus for the trophy defence at Valhalla in 2028.

America need to find something similar, maybe from their recent victorious Curtis Cup team. And, remarkably, that is the only one of the transatlantic trophies that now resides in US hands as the Solheim joins the Ryder and Walker Cups on this side of the pond.

In the Solheim, Europe's newcomers have soaked up the continent's unique bond. It has seeped into their bones and is best summed up by the irrepressible old stager Ciganda.

She might drive you mad with her glacial pace of play, but the veteran Spaniard knows as well as anyone what, for Europe, the Solheim Cup is all about.

"I just love it," Ciganda said. "I love beating the Americans. Yeah, winning for Team Europe, it's the best feeling."

articles.title: Make-A-Wish UK Brings Golf With Your Friends to Life For a Chaotic Charity Stream: How to Watch and What to Expect
articles.body:
Following its hugely successful and award-winning Overcooked! Live charity stream in 2025, Make-A-Wish® UK is back with Golf With Your Friends Live! In collaboration with team17, Golf With Your Friends Live takes the chaotic multiplayer mini golf video game and transforms it into an IRL crowd-controlled crazy golf tournament featuring content creators including TwoAngryGamers, CyborgAngel, Nikoheart and WorstPremadeEver. In this real-life version, the audience is in control of how the game plays out with donations unlocking ‘Goodwill Wishes’ or ‘Mischievous Wishes’ that influence the gameplay in real time!

Co-hosted by comedian, presenter, actor and video game voice artist Inel Tomlinson and returning host, actress, cosplayer and lover of all things nerdy AlicesPixels, the real-life tournament is raising money for Make-A-Wish UK. For children living with critical illness, hospital stays, treatment and uncertainty can make their world feel smaller. Make-A-Wish UK restores what can become lost to illness: the chance to choose, the courage to dream beyond diagnosis, and precious time with family.

Right now, there are around 134,000 children in the UK living with critical illness that could make them eligible for a wish. That’s enough to fill over 11,000 Golf With Your Friends games at the same time. And every hour, another child is diagnosed.

Your donation can grant the wishes that give them their childhood back.

If you want to get involved, here’s how to watch, get involved and what to expect!

How to Watch the Make-A-Wish UK Golf With Your Friends Live Stream

Watch the Make-A-Wish UK Golf With Your Friends Live Stream on Sunday, 20th September at 4pm BST / 11am EST / 8am PST on Tiltify here:

But you don’t have to wait until then to get involved! In fact, you can donate right now via the Tiltify page linked above to influence the first round.

In Golf With Your Friends Live, content creators will be battling it out amongst each other in an attempt to win the tournament and take home the “prestigious” Make-A-Wish Cup ⁠– but it won’t all be holes in one. Viewers watching the stream have the ability to grant advantages, sabotage contestants and alter the rules of the competition, all with the power of donations.

As more donations roll in and milestones are met, gameplay-changing wishes are triggered, so viewers at home can have a hand in creating hilarious and memorable moments throughout the stream.

Such an event is only possible due to the generosity of individuals and companies, including the following: Rob Small (CEO of Miniclip ), Mountain Pictures (Film Crew), Arena Media UK (Media Agency), Supernaut Studio (Creative Agency), and Shed Wilson from Boost Comms (Stage Manager), as well as sponsors Xsolla , Guillotine , Breddos and Patty & Bun .

Behind it all is a dedicated team of gaming industry professionals who are volunteering their time to help run the event, they include: Jinesha Ghandi (Volunteer Lead Producer), Veronika Glova (Volunteer Producer), Sally Kevan ( TVG Events Games Industry Event Specialist). Lauren Shotten (Event Manager), Emily Britt (Veteran Games Industry PR and Events), Sam Possible (Games Marketing Consultant at Jump Economy ) and Paul Bondy (Game Audio Composer at InsideInfo ).

Make a difference by watching and donating during the Make-A-Wish UK Golf With Your Friends Live Stream on Sunday, 20th September at 4pm BST / 11am EST / 8am PST here:

Make-A-Wish UK is a registered charity that was established in the UK in 1986 to create life-changing wishes that revive the childhood that critical illness often takes away. The charity receives no Government funding - registered charity numbers: 295672 in England and Wales, SC037479 in Scotland.

articles.title: Tories pick ex-councillor to contest Starmer's former seat
articles.summary: Ewan Cameron, a Camden councillor from 1998 to 2002, will stand in the by-election on 8 October.
articles.body:
The Conservatives have selected former Camden councillor Ewan Cameron as the party's candidate in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election on 8 October.

The seat became vacant when Sir Keir Starmer stood down as an MP to take a role in international affairs.

Cameron was a councillor for the Belsize ward from 1998 to 2002 and sat on the council's development control committee. He stood again in May's borough elections, finishing 10th of 14 candidates in West Hampstead with 376 votes.

He said he was "honoured" to have been selected to stand in next month's by-election. "This is the community where I have lived, raised my family and call home," he said.

Cameron added: "Under Kemi Badenoch's leadership the Conservative Party has changed, we have clear, fully costed plans to recruit 10,000 more police officers, scrap stamp duty on family homes and cut bills with our Cheap Power Plan.

"That is the message I look forward to campaigning on over the coming weeks."

Cameron will face Camden Council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali for Labour and Green Party leader Zack Polanski.

Nominations close at 16:00 BST on Tuesday.

articles.title: Chacarra y Ayora se estrenan en una concentración del equipo europeo de la Ryder Cup
articles.standfirst: Los jugadores españoles participan este lunes en la concentración en Adare Menor
articles.summary: Los jugadores españoles participan este lunes en la concentración en Adare Menor
articles.body: Los jugadores españoles Eugenio Chacarra y Ángel Ayora participan este lunes en la concentración que el capitán del equipo europeo de la Ryder Cup, el inglés Luke Donald, ha organizado en Adare Menor (Irlanda) para ir preparando la competición bienal contra Estados Unidos, que se disputará en este campo en septiembre de 2027. Chacarra y Ayora son, junto con el inglés Alex Fitzpatrick y el noruego Kristoffer Reitan, los jugadores novatos convocados por primera vez por Donald junto con los que ganaron a Estados Unidos la Ryder Cup el año pasado en Nueva York, entre ellos, el también español Jon Rahm. El madrileño y el malagueño participaron en el Abierto de Irlanda que finalizó ayer, domingo, en Doonbeg y de ahí se desplazaron a Adare Manor, en el condado de Limerick, para estar hoy en la jornada de convivencia, que incluye una ronda de prácticas de 18 hoyos en el campo donde se disputará el enfrentamiento contra EE. UU. Donald dio a conocer la invitación a Chacarra y Ayora la semana pasada en la víspera del torneo irlandés, en el que también participó el capitán, quien tiene el reto de ser el primero en lograr tres victorias consecutivas con Europa coincidiendo con el centenario del torneo. Chacarra, de 26 años y número 58 del mundo, se ha consolidado como una de las figuras emergentes del golf europeo con dos triunfos esta temporada en el DP World Tour, en Países Bajos e Italia, y el tercer puesto en el ránking del circuito, conocido como 'Race to Dubai'), con lo que tiene casi matemáticamente asegurada una tarjeta para el PGA Tour el próximo año. Como prueba del interés que suscitan los dos españoles, Chacarra jugó las dos primeras rondas en Doonbeg junto con el veterano irlandés Padraig Harrington, uno de los vicecapitanes de Donald. Desde Adare Manor, la mayoría de los concentrados viajará a Wentworth, en la periferia de Londres, donde este jueves comienza el torneo el campeonato BMW PGA, uno de los más importantes del DP World Tour del curso. Al equipo europeo de la próxima Ryder Cup acceden los seis mejores en la clasificación específica que se puso en marcha a finales de agosto y otros seis jugadores invitados por Donald, que se conocerán el 30 de agosto de 2027.

articles.title: 'Won't reveal my face, will file FIR today': Gurgaon woman biker issues statement after hit-and-run
articles.summary: GURGAON: Woman biker Sia, whose video alleging a hit-and-run on Golf Course Road went viral on Monday, said she will file an FIR with her lawyer by Mo.
articles.body: GURGAON: Woman biker Sia, whose video alleging a hit-and-run on Golf Course Road went viral on Monday, said she will file an FIR with her lawyer by Monday evening and take legal action in the matter.In an Instagram story, Sia thanked people for their support and said she had seen efforts being made to identify the person involved in the incident. She also said she was receiving requests from news channels and journalists for interviews, but would not be speaking to the media.“I do not wish to reveal my identity or face, and I won't be giving any interviews this time,” Sia said, asking people to respect her decision.She added that she would keep them updated and asked those seeking more information to contact her through Instagram.Sia had earlier shared a video recorded on an action camera mounted on her motorcycle, alleging that a car repeatedly followed her while she was riding with a group of bikers on Sunday before hitting her motorcycle and fleeing.She alleged that the occupants appeared to be intoxicated and that the driver asked her to stop despite her asking him to maintain a safe distance. She said she continued riding ahead as she felt the situation was unsafe.The footage appears to show the car coming into contact with her motorcycle, knocking her off the bike and dragging the motorcycle for several metres before fleeing.Sia said one of her friends chased the car and confronted the driver at a traffic signal. According to her, the driver denied responsibility and drove away.The car owner, Manish, has since told that the vehicle belonged to him but had been borrowed by his friend Kalyan Singh two days earlier.Manish said he was at work and learnt about the accident only on Monday morning. He said Singh did not answer his calls after he tried to contact him.Gurgaon Police has taken suo motu cognisance of the viral video and said the accused would be identified and arrested at the earliest. articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: How Team Europe celebrated win over Team USA and Anna Nordqvist's side delivered home victory
articles.summary: Talking points from Team Europe's Solheim Cup victory over Team USA at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands, including big celebrations after Anna Nordqvist's side impressed on a final day and Charley Hull, Lottie Woad, Carlota Ciganda, Linn Grant all delivered
articles.body:
That was the chant echoing around the Team Europe bus on Sunday evening after another Solheim Cup home success, where Anna Nordqvist overcame Team USA on the final day to regain the trophy.

The contest had been delicately poised heading into a rainy sit singles session at Bernardus Golf, with the momentum seemingly with the Americans after late drama in the Saturday fourballs saw them pull the match back into an 8-8 tie.

Jennifer Kupcho had holed over 110 feet of putts over her final two holes to snatch victory with Lindy Duncan over Carlota Ciganda and Celine Boutier, a result Team USA captain Angela Stanford said had "turned the tide" in their favour.

A video of the American team drinking beers on their bus that evening ended up being a premature celebration and an easy motivator for Team Europe, who won six of the top eight singles matches to regain control of the contest.

Lottie Woad's point-winning moment will be remembered as the one that clinched the Solheim Cup, taking Europe to 14 points with Carlota Ciganda already guaranteed at least a half-point, but it was the Spaniard who closed out her win and made it official.

Boisterous scenes around the course and in the trophy presentation continued off it, with a viral social media clip of Dame Laura Davies handing out beers to the European team on the bus and their celebrations running long into the night.

A final score of 15-13 didn't really reflect the final-day dominance of Nordqvist's side, with Team USA's largely flat top order - Nelly Korda and Alison Lee aside - unable to follow up their jubilance of the previous night and put pressure on Europe.

Few embrace the Solheim Cup more than Ciganda, who went from Europe's first-tee supporter in the opening session to producing multiple clutch moments as the week progressed.

The veteran was Europe's hero on Friday, where a dramatic final-hole par gave her and Julia Lopez Ramirez a half-point that avoided Team USA leading after day one, then was on the receiving end of Kupcho's birdie-birdie finish the following day.

Ciganda gained revenged over Kupcho in the singles and closed out her eighth appearance in style, becoming just the second player in history to earn the clinching point in two different Solheim Cups.

" I was really happy to see that I was playing against Kupcho," Ciganda admitted. "She's a fighter, I'm a fighter. I knew she had no chance. I was like, 'I want to kill you', so I had it very clear in my mind."

Charley Hull and Woad became the first pairing ever to tandem in all four sessions and broke several unwanted records during a disappointing first two days, despite playing better than their scores suggested.

They were both inside the top four for European birdies made over those sessions but returned just 0.5 points, with a record-equalling 6&5 loss in the Saturday morning foursomes among the three defeats.

Nordqvist was questioned for not splitting the pair on day two and came under further scrutiny for sending out Hull in the singles, a decision she described as a "no-brainer" before watching the 30-year-old earn Europe's first point of the day.

Hull said it was a "frustrating" week that saw her and Woad struggle to hole putts, with both - until their singles victories - in danger of becoming the first to participate in five sessions and not have any wins.

"Being the leader of this team, we knew she [Hull] was going to deliver," Nordqvist said. "It was blue on the board early. Lottie [Woad] has been very steady this week - it was nice to see her finally hole some putts"

Grant joins exclusive club as Europe's MVP

Team Europe's star performance came from Linn Grant, who became the first player to go from earning zero points in the previous Solheim Cup to earn at least four points in the next.

Grant became only the ninth player to go 4-0 or better during a Solheim Cup, with three victories alongside Maja Stark followed by a commanding 4&3 win over Angel Yin in the singles.

The all-Swedish pairing between the close friends was also seen in the 2023 edition and likely again in future Solheim Cups, with Grant overcoming shocking pre-event form - having five missed cuts in six starts - to finish as Europe's leading scorer.

"That is a really cool feeling that you have a person like this on your team, that you know you can just go out and you know them inside and out and their game," Stark explained about Grant. "It felt like, for Anna, it was a no-brainer to put us together."

Europe's captain's picks all delivered at least 1.5 points each, with Leona Maguire stepping up - in another record-breaking display - and the other three rookies contributing to push Nordqvist's side to the target required.

Maguire won both foursomes sessions alongside Esther Henseleit to become the quickest player to reach 10 match wins, taking just 14 matches and one faster than the previous record.

She briefly had the highest winning percentage in Solheim Cup history until her loss alongside Celine Boutier in the fourballs, while Ramirez responded to being left out throughout Saturday to finish unbeaten from her two matches.

"I said from the beginning her picks were really good," Stanford insisted, having seen her three picks deliver five points for Team USA. "She picked well because this golf course needed high-ball hitters and that's what she did."

Rhodes shines in 'unexpected' partnership

Had the final round of the AIG Women's Open played out differently last month, Rhodes would likely not have teed it up in the Netherlands. Instead, she leaves this week as a strong Team Europe options for many Solheim Cups ahead.

Henseleit finishing runner-up at Royal Lytham - the final qualifying event - saw her overtake Chiara Tamburlini in the European points list, securing Nanna Koerstz Madsen qualification via the world rankings and freeing up an extra captain's pick.

Rhodes took full advantage and was an instant hit, revelling in the first-tee spotlight and forming a winning partnership in both foursomes and foursomes with Nastasia Nadaud - the first rookie pairing to win two matches together at a Solheim Cup.

"A lot of people questioned why would you send out two rookies, but I said why not?!" Nordqvist explained. "And they delivered. I never felt like they were rookies."

Only Grant ended the week with more points for Team Europe than Nadaud, who was barely inside the world's top 150 a year ago but continued her meteoric rise with a Solheim Cup debut to remember.

A strong friendship off the course with Rhodes fuelled an equally impressive dynamic on it, with their 4&3 foursomes win on Saturday morning matching the largest-winning margin by a rookie pair.

Her performance that morning - where she was surprised to have even been selected - led to her being sent back out with Maguire that day, while her 3&2 singles win over Andrea Lee came at a time where Team USA threatened to wrestle back some control.

"Getting three points for Europe is just absolutely crazy - got no words for that," said Nadaud, who will now have her sights set on representing Europe again in years to come. "Everything just happened so fast!"

It would be little surprise to see the majority of Nordqvist's winning dozen back together in the future to try and win on away soil, given seven of them will still be aged under 30 for the 2028 edition in Virginia.

Four rookies making an immediate impact only highlighted the strength and depth of Europe's options, given the home victory came without recent Solheim Cup regulars Georgia Hall, Emily Kristine Pedersen and Madelene Sagstrom.

It was also the first Solheim Cup since 2007 without Nordqvist being involved as a player, having announced her retirement mid-season and ruling herself out of a captain's pick, but could the Swede be back again in the future?

"You're never going to say never," Nordqvist said in their victory press conference, when asked if she would consider taking on captaincy again in 2028. "I don't know what my future holds."

When Europe last won outright on home soil in 2019, Catriona Matthew returned as captain again to lead them to away glory in the following edition. Whether it's Nordqvist at the wheel or not in Virginia, that will be the next target.

The next edition of the Solheim Cup will be in 2028 and take place at Valhalla Golf Club in Kentucky from September 8-10 that year. Get latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW .

articles.title: Matt LaFleur defends disastrous decision to take points off board before Packers meltdown
articles.summary: Green Bay fell victim to a brutal fourth quarter against the Vikings.
articles.body:
Everything seemed to be going according to plan for the Green Bay Packers in their Week 1 divisional test against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. Jordan Love and the offense were moving the ball at will and it looked like the only thing standing in the way of a season-opening victory was the defense withstanding a late effort by Carson Wentz . Green Bay appeared to take a 25-17 lead with a little over 13 minutes to play in regulation on a Trey Smack field goal. Those points came off the board when Matt LaFleur opted to accept an offsides penalty in favor of a 4th-and-1 and a chance to truly put the game away with a touchdown.

Unfortunately for him, that decision aged poorly as Love was stuffed on a quarterback sneak, allowing the Vikings to take possession. Minnesota would then take the lead and pile on as they posted 22 unanswered points in the final quarter to emerge with a 39-22 victory.

It was a stunning sequence of events for Green Bay and puts them behind the sticks as every other team in the NFC North is off to a 1-0 start.

"I think that's just we're going to be aggressive," he said. "It was going to be an eight-point game. If it would have been a two-possession game, I probably would have thought otherwise. But I thought we had a chance. We didn't do very well in the red zone. . . . Sometimes you live and die by that, but we're gonna be aggressive and we're gonna try to go for the throat in that situation."

To be clear, taking the points off the board did not lose the game by itself. There's no doubt that it set in forth a chain reaction that spelled disaster. But if you're allowing Wentz to score at will, that's a bigger problem and could spell doom for Green Bay's lofty expectations this season.

Still, it's a rough way to start the season as Packers fans are wondering what could have been if they had just taken the three points and preserved momentum.

articles.title: Breaking down Packers' 39-22 loss to Vikings: What went right, wrong
articles.summary: Vikings 39, Packers 22: What went right, what went wrong and what it means for Green Bay.
articles.body:
Hello, darkness, my old friend. The Green Bay Packers collapsed again. Matt LaFleur's team was in full control through 40 minutes of Sunday's season opener, but the Minnesota Vikings scored the game's final 29 points and cruised to a 39-22 victory at U.S. Bank Stadium. After losing five straight games to finish 2025, the Packers are now 0-1 to open 2026.

Here's what went right, what went wrong and what it means for the Packers moving forward:

The Packers outgained the Vikings 419 to 239, highlighting both the supply of explosive plays created by the passing game and the down-to-down effectiveness of Jonathan Gannon's defense. The Packers averaged 6.3 yards per play; the Vikings averaged 3.9. Most weeks, these numbers would reflect a comfortable win for Green Bay . Not on this day.

The Packers certainly weren't perfect through three quarters, but they were clearly the better team entering the fourth quarter. They led 9-0 early, 19-10 at half and held a 22-10 lead late into the third. Unfortunately for Matt LaFleur's team, football games are 60 minutes long.

The passing game showed great potential, with Christian Watson , Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft combining for 307 total receiving yards. When the Packers were able to block up Minnesota's front, Jordan Love consistently hit explosive plays. Watson, Golden and Kraft all had multiple catches of 20+ yards. Jonnu Smith had a 43-yarder.

The Micah Parsons-less pass-rush showed up. The Packers had three sacks and six quarterback hits, and several other pressures were negated by penalty. The Vikings didn't throw the ball often, but Green Bay was able to affect the passer consistently. Lukas Van Ness and Edgerrin Cooper both had sacks.

Brian Flores overwhelmed an overmatched Packers offensive line. Even during a chaotic first half, Jordan Love was only 9-of-19 passing, largely due to all the havoc being caused up front. Flores was relentless calling blitzes, and the Vikings ended up with a pressure rate over 50 percent and 15 total hits on Love. Both of the Packers' turnovers late were the result of immediate pressure. A lack of communication and cohesion up front killed the Packers in big spots.

The Vikings scored five touchdowns: one on a free play when the Packers jumped offsides before the two-minute warning, one after a 68-yard kickoff return, one featuring four defensive penalties (including three negating stops) and two touchdowns on short fields (1-yard line, 14-yard line) following turnovers. The Packers didn't make the Vikings earn their points on Sunday.

The Packers were 1-for-4 scoring touchdowns in the red zone, while the Vikings finished a perfect 4-for-4. Minnesota got 29 points from their four red zone trips. Green Bay got 10. That's a 19-point difference in a 17-point game!

The Packers committed 12 penalties to the Vikings' three, and there was an 83-yard difference in penalty yards between the two teams. On Minnesota's go-ahead drive, the Packers had four penalties.

Not only did the Packers struggle to protect the quarterback, but running the ball was a chore. Green Bay finished with 68 rushing yards on 21 attempts. MarShawn Lloyd averaged only 2.8 yards per attempt. Minnesota had three tackles for loss against the run.

Not being able to get a yard on 4th-and-1 and then collapsing the rest of the way really typifies this stretch of Packers football.

The losing streak extended to six games, the offseason emphasis on finishing didn't translate, and now the Packers are 0-1 to start 2026, with a demoralizing but familiar loss against an NFC North rival. Will this be a confidence-rattling defeat for a team that hasn't tasted a win since early December of last year? In what is shaping up to be another competitive NFC North race, the Packers are the only team in the division entering Week 2 without a win. The concerns along the offensive line were justified, exposing what appears to be a fatal flaw.

Another road trip, this time to play the 1-0 New York Jets in the noon timeslot next Sunday. The Packers have lost five straight road games and haven't won away from home since Thanksgiving Day last year, so any road trip looks like a big challenge. The Jets controlled Week 1 on the road, never trailing before beating the Tennessee Titans 23-10. New York allowed only 195 total yards, and Geno Smith was excellent in his Jets return. The Packers better bring their "A" game to MetLife Stadium next week.
